text:
The University of Melbourne features an extensive academic profile supported by a diverse library system, which serves over three million visitors annually and houses a collection exceeding 3.5 million items. The university maintains twelve libraries across its campuses, with most having a subject focus. Beyond libraries, it hosts several notable museums and archives, including the Grainger Museum (Australia's only purpose-built autobiographical museum), the Harry Brookes Allen Museum of Anatomy and Pathology, and the Ian Potter Museum of Art.
The university's physical presence is spread across multiple campuses: Parkville (the primary campus), Southbank (housing the Victorian College of the Arts), Burnley (for horticulture), and specialized rural campuses in Creswick (forest science) and Dookie (agriculture). In terms of governance, the peak governing body is the Council, and the university is divided into nine faculties, including the Faculty of Arts and the Faculty of Medicine, Dentistry and Health Sciences. Furthermore, the University of Melbourne has established a major capital works program, with a new engineering campus planned for Fishermans Bend starting in 2026.
